title: Triage Sprint — morning notes (serving runtime)
content:
Quick context: woke up to a persistent p99 increase for small-text in prod (hosted-api eu-west) starting ~2025-11-03 22:30 UTC. Spike correlates with a rolling canary of batch-scheduler v2 (partial rollout). Rough aim: triage, gather repros, isolate whether kernel-level scheduling, batching logic, or KV-prefetch evictions are root cause.

Observations (raw):
- p50 stable, p95 slight uptick, p99 +80-120ms for 1-4 token requests.
- Affected route: /v1/generate (small prompts, seq_len <= 32).
- Canary traffic split 10% -> correlates with error window and higher CPU steal on GPU hosts.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 96%->82% for a few nodes. Those nodes match canary tag.
- No OOM, no obvious CUDA mem errors in dmesg. Some intermittent nvlink timeout warnings ~22:40 but cleared.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batch-scheduler v2 change increases tail latency due to occasional micro-batching waits introduced when request arrival patterns are bursty (timing wheel thresholds mis-tuned).
2) KV cache eviction policy change combined with v2 interacts: more cache misses -> longer model init/kv load for short requests -> p99 spike.
3) Underlying host-level scheduler (cgroup/cpuacct) sees new bursty thread patterns -> CPU steal and context-switch penalties -> tail latency.
4) NVLink flakiness during canary causing occasional stall on KV transfer (less likely; only a couple warnings).

Repro plan (local / staging):
- Recreate arrival pattern: small bursts of 20 reqs/0.5s followed by idle 5s. Use load-gen script (see below).
- Deploy batch-scheduler v2 to staging without KV changes -> measure p99. If spike => scheduler.
- Deploy only KV eviction change to staging (old scheduler) -> measure.
- If both individually fine, deploy both -> look for interaction.

Quick load-gen (notes to self):
- load-gen: scripts/perf/load_small_bursts.py (use header X-Canary-Test to hit canary routing).
- curl example: for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Canary-Test: true" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":4}' & done; wait; sleep 5; done
- collect traces: set TRACE_ID env and enable tracing via /internal/trace-toggle (staging).

Telemetry to collect:
- per-request start/end timestamps, batch size, batch enqueue wait time, handler queue length.
- GPU utilization + PCIe/NVLink counters during spike windows.
- KV cache evictions, key load latency histogram.
- host-level metrics: cpu steal, ctx-switches/sec, irq cycles.

Immediate checks I ran (notes):
- inspected canary hosts: system load not high, but context-switch spikes align with p99 windows. top /proc/interrupts looked normal.
- docker stats: ephemeral CPU throttle on container host for short windows.
- loaded /var/log/syslog: a few cgroup reclaim events and docker oom-kill? (false positive, another container evicted earlier at 22:37 unrelated).
- pulled KV metrics from telemetry: eviction rate ~3x normal on canary; miss latency 4-8ms -> previously 0.5-1.2ms.
- checked batch queue histograms: occasional 15-30ms queue waits for micro-batches (we usually aim <5ms).

Short-term mitigations to test:
- rollback batch-scheduler v2 to v1 for canary -> watch p99 for 30m. (Evan to coordinate rollback)
- raise KV cache size for canary nodes by +10% (cheap attempt).
- temporarily increase batch max wait threshold so scheduler doesn't artificially delay tiny bursts.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Make scheduler adaptive to observed inter-arrival jitter instead of fixed windows. Add jitter-sensing mode.
- KV eviction: move to LRU with priority pins for short-payload keys (hotkey protection).
- Improve host isolation: pin scheduler threads to dedicated CPUs, cgroup reservations for critical threads.

Notes / commands useful for debugging (for next run):
- perf top -p <pid> -g --call-graph=dwarf (collect stack for slow handler)
- trace-cmd record -e sched_switch -e sched_wakeup -o /tmp/trace.dat -- sleep 30
- nvprof --systems? (collect only if we reproduce NVLink warnings)
- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/*/cpuacct.usage_percpu

Immediate action items (assigned):
- Keisha: reproduce in staging with burst script, capture traces + batch histograms (today).
- Luca: check scheduler commit diff (batch-scheduler v2) for timing wheel defaults + unit tests around tiny bursts (today).
- Mina: pull KV cache telemetry across canary hosts and compare key access patterns; try +10% cache size experiment (today).
- Evan: coordinate rollback if we confirm v2 correlates (have rollback ready, but hold until morning sync).

Meeting sync (0900 PST): quick 15m to decide rollback or mitigation.

Random brain-dump / TODOs to flesh out later:
- Add a synthetic test in CI that simulates bursty arrival patterns for tiny token requests and fails if p99 > baseline. Could be in smoke tests.
- Add more granular logging for batch decision reasons (why did we wait vs dispatch). Tag logs with decision trace id.
- Consider exposing a per-route batching tuning override in console for quick rollouts.

Questions I want to ask in sync:
- Luca: any obvious change in the batching decision code that would add a timer or more aggressive coalescing?
- Mina: are the hotkeys for these small prompts stable? Is a tiny set of prompts causing cache churn?
- SRE: did we change any host-level daemon config (kubelet, systemd) around the time of canary?

Notes to self (closing):
- keep experiments small and revertible. prioritize rollout safety over micro-optimizations.
- record each experiment start/end with trace-id and link to PR + JIRA.
- follow up EOD with retrospective notes if we rollback or mitigate.

End of morning brain-dump — will update after first staging repro (or after rollback decision).
